findings.issue_text: Imported feed content bypasses the entire sanitization/cooking pipeline (stored XSS): Post#cook returns raw verbatim for :raw_html, TopicEmbed#import feeds remote content into raw with skip_validations, and embed view renders it with raw post.cooked, allowing script injection from feed content
Footer link in TopicEmbed interpolates url unescaped into raw HTML; a URL like http://x/'><script>... passes the ^https?:// guard and breaks out of the attribute, enabling XSS
In the import_remote/readability path, href is preserved by the tag whitelist so javascript: URLs survive sanitization

PollFeed job does not nil-check i.content; SimpleRSS only exposes tags present in the feed, so items using description instead of content:encoded cause nil.scrub to raise NoMethodError, and with retry: false the whole polling run aborts, silently skipping remaining items

absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs: //cdn.example.com/img.png satisfies start_with?('/') and sub(/^\/+/, '') strips all leading slashes, producing a broken link to http://source-host/cdn.example.com/img.png

absolutize_urls ignores plain relative URLs without a leading slash (e.g. images/foo.jpg), leaving them resolving relative to the Discourse embed page and producing broken images/links in imported posts

Non-atomic SETNX/EXPIRE in TopicRetriever: if the process dies between setnx and expire, the key persists forever with no TTL and retrieve refuses to fetch that embed URL for non-staff users indefinitely; should use a single SET key val NX EX 60

Check-then-create race in TopicEmbed.import: the where/first lookup followed by create! is a TOCTOU race; the concurrent loser raises inside Topic.transaction after creating the post, rolling everything back, and in the poll_feed loop (retry: false) that exception aborts remaining items for the hour

embed.js crashes when the mount point is missing: document.getElementById('discourse-comments') result is used without a null check, so comments.appendChild(iframe) throws a TypeError on host pages where the div is absent

Retrieval failures are silent, leaving embed viewers in an infinite reload loop: the loading page reloads every 30 seconds, but TopicRetriever returns silently on permanent failures (missing embed_by_username, failed existence check, import_remote network errors), so the iframe reloads forever with no terminal state

Iframe height measured at window.onload is stale for image-heavy posts: images load after onload so document.body.offsetHeight underestimates final height, and with scrolling="no" the bottom of the discussion is clipped; also the if (parent) check is always true since window.parent is the window itself even when not framed

Unbounded outbound HTTP fetches with no timeout or response size limit in `open(url).read` (lib/topic_retriever.rb:47-53, app/models/topic_embed.rb:46-47), pinning Sidekiq workers on slow/hanging or huge endpoints

Embeddable check only validates the forgeable Referer header in EmbedController#ensure_embeddable (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26), allowing unauthenticated users to enqueue retrieve_topic jobs for arbitrary URLs and exhaust the worker pool (throttle is per-URL, so unique query strings bypass it)
retrieve_topic job is enqueued before the throttle check, so request floods grow the job queue unboundedly even when throttled at execution time

perform_retrieve synchronously executes Jobs::PollFeed inside every embed-retrieval job (lib/topic_retriever.rb:35-41), causing full feed fetch + N-item import per new embed URL with concurrent jobs polling simultaneously with no lock

PollFeed computes a Redis Last-Modified feed_key (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:16) but never reads or writes it — intended conditional GET caching is dead code, so the entire feed is re-downloaded and re-imported hourly

Loading page polls server forever: 30-second document.location.reload() loop in app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:6-11 has no termination condition, causing indefinite reloads when import never succeeds
Non-atomic setnx + expire throttle (lib/topic_retriever.rb:24-31) can permanently wedge a URL if the process dies between calls, leaving a key with no TTL; should use SET key val NX EX 60

Broken origin check in public postMessage protocol (embed.js:16-18): substring check `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is spoofable — attacker origin like `http://eviltrout.com.evil.com` passes, letting arbitrary pages control the embed frame's dimensions via resize messages

Unescaped `request.referer` interpolated into inline JavaScript in embed.html.erb:9-12: raw Referer header into single-quoted JS string allows script injection via crafted referer path/query, and absent referer renders `null` as invalid postMessage targetOrigin breaking the resize handshake

Removal of public CLI option `--category` from disqus import Thor task (lib/tasks/disqus.thor:114-149) with no deprecation or replacement, causing existing invocations to hard-fail with 'Unknown option' error

Resize handshake only fires at `window.onload` (embed.html.erb:9-12, embed.js:20-23) with no repeated resize mechanism, so iframe height goes stale when content (e.g., images) grows after load and clipped content is unreachable with `scrolling="no"`

Loading view (loading.html.erb:1-12) reloads every 30 seconds forever with no terminal/error state — when TopicRetriever#retrieve bails (host mismatch, missing embed_by_username, fetch failure, or throttle), the iframe loops reloads indefinitely and embedders can't distinguish 'still importing' from 'will never work'

Every anonymous embed view enqueues a background job with no dedup (embed_controller.rb:11-12): Jobs.enqueue runs before throttle/existence check, so a hot link or misconfigured embeddable_host causes one Sidekiq job per visitor hit

poll_feed (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:33-36) assumes every feed item has `content` and raises NoMethodError for feeds with only description/summary; with retry: false the exception kills the scheduled run and permanently stalls the feed at that entry

Embed snippet contract is fragile (embed.js:1-9): throws uncaught TypeError if `#discourse-comments` doesn't exist, throws if discourseUrl/discourseEmbedUrl globals are missing, and string-concatenates discourseUrl without handling missing trailing slash, silently requesting the wrong URL

Embed responses cache the 'loading' state (embed_controller.rb:15): the 1-minute cache header applies to the loading branch too, so intermediaries can serve the loading page for up to a minute after the topic exists

P1: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:28 — open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) has no open_timeout/read_timeout and no rescue, so a stalled feed host can hang the Sidekiq worker indefinitely; combined with retry: false a single flaky fetch silently loses the entire poll cycle with no backoff or alerting

P1: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:33-38 — no per-item rescue: i.content is nil on valid feeds (summary/description-only items), causing nil.scrub NoMethodError that aborts the loop; with retry: false items after the bad one are skipped, and a permanently malformed item causes polling to fail on every run with no error surfaced; a TopicEmbed.import/DB error on item 1 likewise prevents items 2..n from processing

P2: lib/topic_retriever.rb:29-35 — non-atomic SETNX+EXPIRE leaves the retrieved_key with no TTL if the process dies between the two calls, permanently wedging the throttle so the URL can never be fetched again until the key is manually deleted; should use a single atomic SET key val NX EX 60

P2: app/models/topic_embed.rb:47-53 (via lib/topic_retriever.rb:51) — TopicEmbed.import_remote uses open(url).read with no timeout and no error handling, allowing a slow site to hang the RetrieveTopic job unboundedly; transient failures raise into Sidekiq retries where the 60s throttle key makes the first several retries silent no-ops, wasting the retry budget and potentially never fetching the embed

P2: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:6-10 and app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9-12 — the loading page retries forever with no terminal error state, reloading every 30 seconds and re-enqueueing a retrieve_topic job each time; staff users pass no_throttle: true so an open staff tab enqueues a job every 30 seconds indefinitely, each performing an untimed HTTP fetch of the failing URL

P3: app/models/topic_embed.rb:20-24 — TopicEmbed.import silently swallows post-creation failure: if PostCreator fails, post is nil, no TopicEmbed row is created, and the method returns nil with no logging or error raised, so on the RetrieveTopic/import_remote path the failure is silent and never retried (user sees 'Loading...' forever)

P3: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41-44 — Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) runs synchronously inside the RetrieveTopic job, so one embed request can trigger a full feed fetch and import of many articles inline, dramatically extending job runtime and coupling embed retrieval to the health of the entire external feed

P0: Migration sets cook_method default: 1 (raw_html) so every post defaults to raw_html and Post#cook returns raw for all posts, and no test pins that a post with the default cook_method still goes through the normal cooking pipeline (would be caught by a test asserting a regular post's cooked output differs from its raw markdown)

P1: Controller specs verify mock wiring, not real behavior; the embed rendering path (app/views/embed/best.html.erb and layouts/embed.html.erb postMessage resize handshake) is never executed by any test, and there is no request/integration spec for /embed/best end-to-end

P1: post_revisor behavioral change (skip_validations now actually suppresses validation on save) with zero test coverage: no test that skip_validations: true saves an invalid post nor that the default path still validates

P2: topic_retriever_spec stubs the methods it should be testing (retrieved_recently?), leaving the Redis setnx/expire throttle, the 60s expiry, the no_throttle staff bypass, perform_retrieve's already-exists bail check, Jobs::PollFeed invocation, and fetch_http's silent return when embed_by_username has no matching user untested

P2: poll_feed_spec tests only the gating via mock expectation, never the feed-processing body: RSS parsing, the url fallback for Atom tag-URI ids, CGI.unescapeHTML on scrubbed content (raises NoMethodError on Atom entries with no content element, killing the hourly job with retry: false), and the silent return when the configured username doesn't exist

P2: TopicEmbed.import re-import with unchanged content (content_sha1 no-op branch) is untested, and the update test doesn't assert content_sha1 persistence or that no duplicate TopicEmbed/topic is created (unique index on embed_url makes a duplicate-creation regression a hard 500)
P2: TopicEmbed.import_remote has no test at all (readability options, doc.title fallback)
P2: TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls port handling untested for non-80/443 ports and scheme-less URLs

P2: New job Jobs::RetrieveTopic has no spec covering the Discourse::InvalidParameters raise on blank embed_url, the user lookup, and forwarding no_throttle: user.try(:staff?) (the security-relevant staff/non-staff throttle branch)

P2: No hostile-input tests for the raw-HTML import path: embed_url is interpolated unescaped into an <a href> in raw_html content rendered with raw, and no tests cover embed_url or feed content containing quotes/HTML/script (e.g. http://host/x'><script>...)
P3: Client-side embed code (embed.js iframe injection and postMessage resize handshake including the discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) origin check and echoing request.referer) has no qunit/JS coverage

P3: disqus.thor import rewritten to fetch each thread's live remote URL via TopicEmbed.import_remote (and --category option removed) with zero test or spec coverage for this behavioral change to a data-migration tool

External HTML rendered completely unsanitized: Post#cook returns raw verbatim when cook_method == :raw_html, skipping the entire cooking pipeline including sanitization, and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, causing stored XSS on the forum's origin (app/models/post.rb:131-134, app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19)

Unescaped URL interpolated into stored HTML in TopicEmbed: the imported-from footer builds HTML by string concatenation with the untrusted url, allowing attribute breakout via quotes or '>' and resulting in stored raw HTML (app/models/topic_embed.rb:8)

CGI.unescapeHTML actively de-escapes untrusted feed content before storage in PollFeed, converting properly escaped entities like <script> into live script tags and defeating any downstream sanitization layer (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:33)

Reverse-direction origin check in embed client: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` tests whether the incoming origin is a substring of discourseUrl instead of validating e.origin against discourseUrl, a known-broken pattern that also misbehaves with trailing slashes or paths (app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17)

TopicRetriever synchronously instantiates the scheduled PollFeed job and calls execute({}) directly, a separation-of-concerns violation where a single user-triggered embed request causes a full inline feed fetch/parse/import of every item (lib/topic_retriever.rb:38)

Embed loading page reloads forever with no failure path: if RetrieveTopic fails (network error, unparseable feed, unresolved embed_by_username) and PollFeed is retry: false, the iframe shows 'Loading...' and reloads every 30 seconds indefinitely with no backoff, terminal state, or error feedback (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:5-9, app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:9)

PollFeed assumes i.content is present for all feed items: `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError on feeds whose entries lack content (e.g. Atom entries with only summary), and combined with retry: false one malformed item aborts the entire poll cycle (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:33)

skip_validations option leaks from embed import into the generic revision path: PostRevisor exposes `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` as a general-purpose escape hatch allowing any caller to silently bypass all validations on post edits, with nothing marking the revised post as system-authored (lib/post_revisor.rb:85)

Duplicated 'find the embed author user' logic in TopicRetriever and PollFeed: identical User lookup by embed_by_username duplicated in two components, both silently returning nil and doing nothing when the setting doesn't match a real user, with no logging or error on misconfiguration (lib/topic_retriever.rb:50, app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:26)

TopicEmbed.import mutates its caller's contents argument via `contents << ...`, so the caller's variable silently includes the appended footer after the call — pure side-effect coupling in a public model API (app/models/topic_embed.rb:8)

Disqus import task interface silently broken: the --category option is removed without deprecation or version bump, breaking existing scripted invocations with -c, and the task's semantics changed from importing stored Disqus content to fetching the live thread URL via TopicEmbed.import_remote, coupling a one-shot migration tool to network availability (lib/tasks/disqus.thor:114)

Embed client assumes #discourse-comments exists: no null check on document.getElementById('discourse-comments'), so a snippet pasted with the wrong element id throws instead of degrading gracefully (app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:5-10)

Editing already-applied migration 20131223171005_create_top_topics to add force: true to create_table, which will DROP TABLE IF EXISTS on re-run and silently destroy all top_topics data with no rollback path

add_column :posts, :cook_method with default and null: false on the large posts table triggers a full table rewrite under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock in PostgreSQL, blocking all reads/writes with no disable_ddl_transaction! or batching, causing production outage risk on upgrades

create_table :topic_embeds with force: true will drop and recreate the table if re-run after embeddings exist, destroying the embed_url → topic mapping and causing duplicate re-imports with no down-guard or pre-drop data check

t.string :embed_url maps to varchar(255), so long real-world URLs will raise ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid on insert, aborting the PollFeed job mid-iteration (retry: false) and permanently skipping remaining feed items with no later migration widening the column

Stored XSS: externally-authored RSS/Atom feed HTML imported via raw_html cook path with zero sanitization, bypassing the entire cooking pipeline and rendering executable HTML via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in embed/best.html.erb and topic pages
Readability import path strips script tags but does not filter URL schemes, so `href="javascript:..."` on allowed `<a>` tags survives into cooked HTML

Unescaped URL interpolated into href attribute in TopicEmbed.import (topic_embed.rb:11); URL validated only by a prefix regex, allowing quotes/HTML to break out of the attribute and inject persistent HTML

Unauthenticated /embed/best acts as a job-enqueue and outbound-fetch amplifier; the Referer header check provides no real protection and per-URL throttling is bypassed by cycling URLs, flooding Sidekiq, performing outbound fetches, and writing Redis keys

PollFeed fails silently and permanently: retry: false with no error handling means nil feed fields (i.content, i.title) crash the run, one malformed item skips all subsequent items forever, and blank titles bypass validations due to skip_validations: true
TopicEmbed.import raises RecordNotUnique on concurrent first-retrievals of the same embed_url against the unique index, killing the remaining feed items for that run

Embed loading page reloads forever when retrieval silently no-ops (e.g. blank embed_by_username or fetch failure), generating steady background load and outbound fetches with no surfaced misconfiguration
Non-atomic SETNX/EXPIRE in TopicRetriever (lib/topic_retriever.rb:31-37) can permanently blacklist an embed URL if the process crashes between the two calls, since the key persists with no TTL
embed.js origin check uses indexOf substring match instead of strict origin comparison, allowing spoofed origins that are substrings of discourseUrl to post messages
request.referer interpolated raw into a JS single-quoted string in embed.html.erb; Rails html_escape does not escape single quotes, allowing Referer header to break out of the JS string literal
feed_key in poll_feed.rb is dead code: never read or written, no If-Modified-Since/etag handling, so every run re-parses the full feed and the first poll imports the entire backlog

Case-sensitive host comparison in embed_controller.rb and topic_retriever.rb rejects legitimate embedders; URI.host preserves case and excludes port, so differing casing or a port in embeddable_host breaks the comparison
Disqus import task silently drops threads whose link is not http(s); import returns nil and the if post.present? check skips the thread and all its comments with no warning

adjudication_records.issue_text: Imported feed content bypasses the entire sanitization/cooking pipeline (stored XSS): Post#cook returns raw verbatim for :raw_html, TopicEmbed#import feeds remote content into raw with skip_validations, and embed view renders it with raw post.cooked, allowing script injection from feed content

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a :raw_html cook_method that bypasses the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline: Post#cook now `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb). TopicEmbed.import creates posts from remote/RSS contents with `skip_validations: true` and `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/topic_embed.rb), and the RSS poller feeds `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` directly into TopicEmbed.import (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) with no sanitization step shown. The embed view renders the result using `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). Together this allows remote feed content containing e.g. `<script>` or event handlers to be stored and rendered verbatim under the Discourse origin, which is a stored XSS vector.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Footer link in TopicEmbed interpolates url unescaped into raw HTML; a URL like http://x/'><script>... passes the ^https?:// guard and breaks out of the attribute, enabling XSS

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the footer is built by interpolating `url` directly into a raw HTML string: `I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")`. The only guard is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes or angle brackets, so a URL like `http://x/'>

adjudication_records.issue_text: In the import_remote/readability path, href is preserved by the tag whitelist so javascript: URLs survive sanitization

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, `Readability::Document.new` is configured to keep `<a>` tags and preserve the `href` attribute (`tags: ... a ...`, `attributes: %w[href src]`). The extracted `doc.content` is then imported via `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim for `raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline, and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Therefore a `javascript:` URL in an imported `<a href>` would be persisted and output as-is, creating an XSS/unsafe link vector in the embed content.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying bug: calling `i.content.scrub` without ensuring `i.content` exists. The candidate explicitly notes feeds may provide `description` instead of `content:encoded`, leading to `nil.scrub`/NoMethodError, which aligns with the golden expectation to add a description fallback to avoid crashes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs: //cdn.example.com/img.png satisfies start_with?('/') and sub(/^\/+/, '') strips all leading slashes, producing a broken link to http://source-host/cdn.example.com/img.png

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, both `href` and `src` are rewritten when `start_with?('/')`. Protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/img.png` also satisfy this condition, and `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both leading slashes, producing `"#{prefix}/cdn.example.com/img.png"` (e.g., `http://source-host/cdn.example.com/img.png`), which is incorrect and breaks the link. This behavior is directly introduced by the new absolutize logic in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: absolutize_urls ignores plain relative URLs without a leading slash (e.g. images/foo.jpg), leaving them resolving relative to the Discourse embed page and producing broken images/links in imported posts

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, both the anchor and image rewrites only run when `href/src.start_with?('/')` (root-relative). Plain relative URLs like `images/foo.jpg` or `../foo` are not converted, despite the method comment saying it converts relative URLs to absolute. Such URLs would then resolve relative to the Discourse embed page path, likely breaking links/images in imported posts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic SETNX/EXPIRE in TopicRetriever: if the process dies between setnx and expire, the key persists forever with no TTL and retrieve refuses to fetch that embed URL for non-staff users indefinitely; should use a single SET key val NX EX 60

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle uses two separate Redis calls: `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes or is killed after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will remain without a TTL and `retrieved_recently?` will keep returning true, preventing future retrieval for that `@embed_url` for non-staff users. This is a real correctness issue introduced by the diff; using a single atomic `SET ... NX EX 60` (or a Lua script) would avoid it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Check-then-create race in TopicEmbed.import: the where/first lookup followed by create! is a TOCTOU race; the concurrent loser raises inside Topic.transaction after creating the post, rolling everything back, and in the poll_feed loop (retry: false) that exception aborts remaining items for the hour

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, enters a `Topic.transaction` and eventually does `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)`. Since the migration adds `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`, concurrent callers can both observe `embed.blank?` and then the “loser” will hit a uniqueness violation on `create!` (TOCTOU race). There is no rescue around this in `TopicEmbed.import` or in the `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` loop (`rss.items.each ... TopicEmbed.import(...)`), and `PollFeed` sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so such an exception would abort the job and stop processing remaining feed items for that run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js crashes when the mount point is missing: document.getElementById('discourse-comments') result is used without a null check, so comments.appendChild(iframe) throws a TypeError on host pages where the div is absent

adjudication.rationale: In new `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, `comments` is set via `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then used immediately in `comments.appendChild(iframe);` with no null check. If the host page does not include an element with id `discourse-comments`, this will throw a `TypeError` at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Retrieval failures are silent, leaving embed viewers in an infinite reload loop: the loading page reloads every 30 seconds, but TopicRetriever returns silently on permanent failures (missing embed_by_username, failed existence check, import_remote network errors), so the iframe reloads forever with no terminal state

adjudication.rationale: The embed UX can get stuck in a perpetual loading/reload loop with no terminal error state. `EmbedController#best` renders `loading` whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil and enqueues `:retrieve_topic` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). The loading template unconditionally reloads every 30s (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb). However `TopicRetriever#retrieve` can return without creating an embed in permanent-config/error cases, e.g. `invalid_host?` returns true when `URI(@embed_url).host` doesn’t match `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (lib/topic_retriever.rb), and `fetch_http` returns if the posting user lookup fails (`username_lower` doesn’t exist / `embed_by_username` is blank-string), meaning no `TopicEmbed` is ever created. In those cases `topic_id_for_embed` stays nil and the iframe keeps reloading forever.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Iframe height measured at window.onload is stale for image-heavy posts: images load after onload so document.body.offsetHeight underestimates final height, and with scrolling="no" the bottom of the discussion is clipped; also the if (parent) check is always true since window.parent is the window itself even when not framed

adjudication.rationale: In the iframe layout (`app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`), the resize message is sent from `window.onload`, which (per browser behavior) fires after the document and its subresources like `` elements have finished loading, so the claim that “images load after onload” making `document.body.offsetHeight` stale is not supported by what’s in the diff. The note that `if (parent)` is always truthy is technically correct, but the diff doesn’t show this causing the reported clipping/broken behavior on its own (and the controller rejects requests with no/invalid referer anyway).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded outbound HTTP fetches with no timeout or response size limit in `open(url).read` (lib/topic_retriever.rb:47-53, app/models/topic_embed.rb:46-47), pinning Sidekiq workers on slow/hanging or huge endpoints

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces outbound HTTP fetches via Ruby's `open-uri` without any explicit timeouts or size limits: `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` and `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`. These are invoked from Sidekiq jobs (`Jobs::RetrieveTopic` -> `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` -> `import_remote`, and scheduled `PollFeed`), so slow/hanging endpoints or very large responses can block/pin workers, constituting a real availability defect exposed by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Embeddable check only validates the forgeable Referer header in EmbedController#ensure_embeddable (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26), allowing unauthenticated users to enqueue retrieve_topic jobs for arbitrary URLs and exhaust the worker pool (throttle is per-URL, so unique query strings bypass it)

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, any request that passes `ensure_embeddable` will enqueue `:retrieve_topic` when no `TopicEmbed` exists (`Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)`). `ensure_embeddable` only checks `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and sets `X-Frame-Options = ALLOWALL`; it does not authenticate the caller or validate `params[:embed_url]` there. Since `Referer` is a client-supplied header, a non-embedded/unauthenticated client can forge it to pass the check and enqueue many jobs. Additionally, throttling in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` is keyed by the full `@embed_url` (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so varying query strings (on the allowed host) bypasses the 60s throttle and forces repeated fetch/import work, enabling worker/queue exhaustion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: retrieve_topic job is enqueued before the throttle check, so request floods grow the job queue unboundedly even when throttled at execution time

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when no TopicEmbed exists it unconditionally enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` on every request (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). The throttle logic (`retrieved_recently?`) is only applied inside `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, which runs when the job executes (lib/topic_retriever.rb + app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb). Nothing in the controller or enqueue path prevents repeated requests for the same `embed_url` from adding unlimited jobs to the queue, even though most executions may no-op due to the throttle. This can cause unbounded job-queue growth under request floods.

adjudication_records.issue_text: perform_retrieve synchronously executes Jobs::PollFeed inside every embed-retrieval job (lib/topic_retriever.rb:35-41), causing full feed fetch + N-item import per new embed URL with concurrent jobs polling simultaneously with no lock

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#perform_retrieve, when SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled? is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously before doing the direct HTTP fetch. Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed fetches the entire feed via `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates all items importing each (`rss.items.each ... TopicEmbed.import`). The only throttling in TopicRetriever is per-embed_url (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so concurrent retrievals for different embed URLs can all trigger a full feed poll with no shared lock/throttle. This is a concrete performance/architecture concern grounded in the diff; it’s not necessarily an immediate correctness defect in all cases, but it can cause redundant work and load under concurrency.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed computes a Redis Last-Modified feed_key (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:16) but never reads or writes it — intended conditional GET caching is dead code, so the entire feed is re-downloaded and re-imported hourly

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` is defined (computes `"feed-modified:..."`) but is never referenced by `execute` or `poll_feed`, and the feed is fetched via `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no Redis read/write. So the review point that this key is dead code is verifiable. However, the claim that the feed is "re-imported hourly" overstates impact: `TopicEmbed.import` de-duplicates by `embed_url` and `content_sha1`, so unchanged items should not be re-created/updated, though the feed is still re-downloaded and iterated each hour.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Loading page polls server forever: 30-second document.location.reload() loop in app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:6-11 has no termination condition, causing indefinite reloads when import never succeeds

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/embed/loading.html.erb the script unconditionally calls document.location.reload() every 30 seconds with no counter/timeout or error handling, so if TopicEmbed creation never happens (e.g., retrieve job fails or can’t import), the iframe will keep reloading indefinitely and repeatedly hitting the server.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic setnx + expire throttle (lib/topic_retriever.rb:24-31) can permanently wedge a URL if the process dies between calls, leaving a key with no TTL; should use SET key val NX EX 60

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently? the throttle uses `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These are non-atomic; if the process crashes or is interrupted after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire`, the key will persist without a TTL, causing `retrieved_recently?` to return true forever for that `@embed_url` (permanent wedge of retrieval). Using a single atomic `SET key val NX EX 60` (or a Lua script/multi) would avoid this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Broken origin check in public postMessage protocol (embed.js:16-18): substring check `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is spoofable — attacker origin like `http://eviltrout.com.evil.com` passes, letting arbitrary pages control the embed frame's dimensions via resize messages

Unescaped `request.referer` interpolated into inline JavaScript in embed.html.erb:9-12: raw Referer header into single-quoted JS string allows script injection via crafted referer path/query, and absent referer renders `null` as invalid postMessage targetOrigin breaking the resize handshake

Removal of public CLI option `--category` from disqus import Thor task (lib/tasks/disqus.thor:114-149) with no deprecation or replacement, causing existing invocations to hard-fail with 'Unknown option' error

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the Thor CLI option `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and also deletes the associated `category_id` lookup/usage. With this change, any existing invocation that passes `--category`/`-c` will now raise Thor's `Unknown option` error (hard-fail), and the diff shows no deprecation path or replacement option.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Resize handshake only fires at `window.onload` (embed.html.erb:9-12, embed.js:20-23) with no repeated resize mechanism, so iframe height goes stale when content (e.g., images) grows after load and clipped content is unreachable with `scrolling="no"`

adjudication.rationale: The iframe resize message is indeed only sent once (layouts/embed.html.erb sets window.onload to post a single {type:'discourse-resize'} message, and embed.js only adjusts height when such a message arrives). However, the finding’s claim that height will go stale specifically because images/content grow *after* load isn’t verifiable from the diff: the embed content is server-rendered/static, and `window.onload` in the iframe fires after page resources (including images) finish loading, so the computed `document['body'].offsetHeight` should already reflect image-loaded layout in the normal case. No dynamic post-load DOM growth mechanism is shown in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Loading view (loading.html.erb:1-12) reloads every 30 seconds forever with no terminal/error state — when TopicRetriever#retrieve bails (host mismatch, missing embed_by_username, fetch failure, or throttle), the iframe loops reloads indefinitely and embedders can't distinguish 'still importing' from 'will never work'

adjudication.rationale: The loading template unconditionally does `setTimeout(... document.location.reload(), 30000)` (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb), and EmbedController#best renders this view whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil. In those cases it also enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`, but the retrieval path can no-op permanently (e.g., TopicRetriever#retrieve returns without fetching when `invalid_host?` is true because `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host`, or `fetch_http` returns when `embed_by_username` user is blank). Since no terminal state is rendered, the iframe will keep reloading indefinitely with no way to distinguish “still importing” from “will never work.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: Every anonymous embed view enqueues a background job with no dedup (embed_controller.rb:11-12): Jobs.enqueue runs before throttle/existence check, so a hot link or misconfigured embeddable_host causes one Sidekiq job per visitor hit

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil, the controller unconditionally calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` on every request before any throttling/deduplication (`app/controllers/embed_controller.rb`). The throttle/existence checks happen later inside `TopicRetriever#retrieve` (Redis `setnx` in `retrieved_recently?`, and `TopicEmbed.where(...).exists?` in `perform_retrieve`), i.e., after the job is already enqueued, so a popular embed URL can still create many Sidekiq jobs that quickly no-op. However, the finding’s claim about a “misconfigured embeddable_host” causing enqueues is not supported because `ensure_embeddable` raises if `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` is blank or the referer host doesn’t match, preventing the enqueue in those cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:33-36) assumes every feed item has `content` and raises NoMethodError for feeds with only description/summary; with retry: false the exception kills the scheduled run and permanently stalls the feed at that entry

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the loop unconditionally does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`; if a feed item lacks `content` (common for RSS items that only provide `description`/`summary`), `i.content` will be nil and `nil.scrub` will raise NoMethodError. With `sidekiq_options retry: false`, that exception will cause the scheduled run to fail (and likely fail again on subsequent runs until the feed/item changes).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Embed snippet contract is fragile (embed.js:1-9): throws uncaught TypeError if `#discourse-comments` doesn't exist, throws if discourseUrl/discourseEmbedUrl globals are missing, and string-concatenates discourseUrl without handling missing trailing slash, silently requesting the wrong URL

adjudication.rationale: In new `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the code unconditionally does `var comments = document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then `comments.appendChild(iframe);` which will throw a TypeError if the element is missing. It also directly references `discourseUrl` and `discourseEmbedUrl` (only declared via `/* global */` comments), which will raise a runtime ReferenceError if those globals are not defined by the embedding page. Finally, `iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."` assumes `discourseUrl` ends with a trailing slash; without it the generated URL is malformed (e.g. `https://forum.example.comembed/best...`). These are concrete, diff-grounded failure modes introduced by this file.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Embed responses cache the 'loading' state (embed_controller.rb:15): the 1-minute cache header applies to the loading branch too, so intermediaries can serve the loading page for up to a minute after the topic exists

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is executed unconditionally after both branches. When `topic_id` is nil, the action renders `'loading'`, but still gets the same 1-minute cache header. That means clients/proxies can legitimately cache and serve the loading page for up to a minute even after the topic has been created, causing stale/broken embed behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:28 — open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) has no open_timeout/read_timeout and no rescue, so a stalled feed host can hang the Sidekiq worker indefinitely; combined with retry: false a single flaky fetch silently loses the entire poll cycle with no backoff or alerting

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the job does `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with `require 'open-uri'` and no `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` options and no exception handling around the network call. A slow or stalled feed endpoint can block the scheduled Sidekiq worker thread for an unbounded time, and because the job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, transient failures (timeouts, socket errors, parse errors) will also abort the poll without any retry/backoff within Sidekiq. This is a real reliability/correctness risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:33-38 — no per-item rescue: i.content is nil on valid feeds (summary/description-only items), causing nil.scrub NoMethodError that aborts the loop; with retry: false items after the bad one are skipped, and a permanently malformed item causes polling to fail on every run with no error surfaced; a TopicEmbed.import/DB error on item 1 likewise prevents items 2..n from processing

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the loop does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and then `TopicEmbed.import(...)` with no per-item guarding. From the diff, if `i.content` is nil (e.g., feeds that only provide description/summary), `nil.scrub` will raise NoMethodError and abort the entire `rss.items.each` loop. Likewise, `TopicEmbed.import` can raise (it calls `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction), which would also abort the loop and prevent later items from processing. With `sidekiq_options retry: false`, a single bad item causes that run to stop processing remaining items and can cause repeated hourly failures on every run if the malformed item persists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: lib/topic_retriever.rb:29-35 — non-atomic SETNX+EXPIRE leaves the retrieved_key with no TTL if the process dies between the two calls, permanently wedging the throttle so the URL can never be fetched again until the key is manually deleted; should use a single atomic SET key val NX EX 60

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb retrieved_recently? uses two separate Redis calls: `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes or is interrupted after SETNX succeeds but before EXPIRE runs, the key will persist without a TTL, causing `retrieved_recently?` to return true forever for that embed URL and permanently preventing retrieval until the key is manually deleted. This is a real correctness/availability bug in the newly added throttle logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: app/models/topic_embed.rb:47-53 (via lib/topic_retriever.rb:51) — TopicEmbed.import_remote uses open(url).read with no timeout and no error handling, allowing a slow site to hang the RetrieveTopic job unboundedly; transient failures raise into Sidekiq retries where the 60s throttle key makes the first several retries silent no-ops, wasting the retry budget and potentially never fetching the embed

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicEmbed.import_remote` which does `open(url).read` with no timeout options and no exception handling (app/models/topic_embed.rb:47-53). This is invoked from `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` (lib/topic_retriever.rb:49-52) inside the `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` path. Additionally, `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` sets the Redis throttle key before any network fetch and will short-circuit subsequent `retrieve` calls for 60s (lib/topic_retriever.rb:23-41). So if `open(url).read` hangs or raises, the job can block a worker unboundedly or fail and then retries within the 60s window may become silent no-ops due to the throttle key, wasting retries and delaying/possibly preventing a successful fetch. This behavior is directly implied by the new code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:6-10 and app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9-12 — the loading page retries forever with no terminal error state, reloading every 30 seconds and re-enqueueing a retrieve_topic job each time; staff users pass no_throttle: true so an open staff tab enqueues a job every 30 seconds indefinitely, each performing an untimed HTTP fetch of the failing URL

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a loading view that unconditionally reloads every 30s (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:6-10). In EmbedController#best, when no TopicEmbed exists it enqueues `:retrieve_topic` on every request and renders that loading page (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9-12). On each reload, the same job is re-enqueued again until the embed succeeds; there is no terminal error state. Additionally, `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` passes `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)`, and `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` explicitly disables throttling when `no_throttle` is true, so a logged-in staff user with the loading page open can cause repeated retrieves every 30s. The retrieve path ultimately does `open(url).read` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` without any explicit timeouts, so failures/hangs can lead to repeated expensive/blocked fetches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: app/models/topic_embed.rb:20-24 — TopicEmbed.import silently swallows post-creation failure: if PostCreator fails, post is nil, no TopicEmbed row is created, and the method returns nil with no logging or error raised, so on the RetrieveTopic/import_remote path the failure is silent and never retried (user sees 'Loading...' forever)

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the new-topic path does `post = creator.create` and only creates the TopicEmbed row if `post.present?` (app/models/topic_embed.rb around the `if embed.blank?` block). If `PostCreator#create` returns nil/blank (without raising), the transaction completes with no TopicEmbed record and the method returns `post` (nil) with no logging/exception. From the embed flow, EmbedController#best will render `loading` whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` stays nil, so a silent create failure can leave the client stuck reloading with no diagnostic signal.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41-44 — Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) runs synchronously inside the RetrieveTopic job, so one embed request can trigger a full feed fetch and import of many articles inline, dramatically extending job runtime and coupling embed retrieval to the health of the entire external feed

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#perform_retrieve, when SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled? is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline (synchronously) before falling back to `fetch_http`. Since EmbedController enqueues `:retrieve_topic` when no embed exists (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb), a single embed request can cause the RetrieveTopic job to synchronously fetch/parse the entire feed and iterate `rss.items.each` importing topics (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb), potentially making the job slow and coupling embed retrieval to external feed performance. This is a legitimate architecture/performance concern grounded in the diff, not a correctness defect per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P0: Migration sets cook_method default: 1 (raw_html) so every post defaults to raw_html and Post#cook returns raw for all posts, and no test pins that a post with the default cook_method still goes through the normal cooking pipeline (would be caught by a test asserting a regular post's cooked output differs from its raw markdown)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Post.cook_methods ||= Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` and the migration sets `posts.cook_method` default to `1`. In this codebase, `Enum.new` is already used for `Post.types` and is typically 1-based (i.e., the first symbol maps to 1). That makes default `1` correspond to `:regular`, not `:raw_html`, so it would not cause all posts to return `raw` from `Post#cook`. The claim that default `1` is `raw_html` is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Controller specs verify mock wiring, not real behavior; the embed rendering path (app/views/embed/best.html.erb and layouts/embed.html.erb postMessage resize handshake) is never executed by any test, and there is no request/integration spec for /embed/best end-to-end

adjudication.rationale: The added controller spec (`spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`) asserts interactions/mocking (`TopicEmbed.expects(:topic_id_for_embed)`, `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)`, `TopicView.expects(:new)`) but does not enable `render_views`, so the newly added templates (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`) and their JS resize `postMessage` handshake are not exercised. The diff also contains no request/integration spec hitting the `get 'embed/best' => 'embed#best'` route end-to-end.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: post_revisor behavioral change (skip_validations now actually suppresses validation on save) with zero test coverage: no test that skip_validations: true saves an invalid post nor that the default path still validates

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes PostRevisor behavior: in lib/post_revisor.rb `@post.save` becomes `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, meaning `skip_validations: true` now actually bypasses model validations. While this option is exercised indirectly (e.g., TopicEmbed.import calls `revisor.revise!(..., skip_validations: true, ...)`), the added specs do not assert validation behavior (no test that an invalid post can be saved with `skip_validations: true`, nor that the default path still validates). This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test/coverage concern rather than a verified runtime bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: topic_retriever_spec stubs the methods it should be testing (retrieved_recently?), leaving the Redis setnx/expire throttle, the 60s expiry, the no_throttle staff bypass, perform_retrieve's already-exists bail check, Jobs::PollFeed invocation, and fetch_http's silent return when embed_by_username has no matching user untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new nontrivial throttling/guard logic in `lib/topic_retriever.rb` (`retrieved_recently?` uses `$redis.setnx`/`expire` with 60s TTL and a `no_throttle` bypass; `perform_retrieve` bails if `TopicEmbed` already exists, may run `Jobs::PollFeed` and then `fetch_http`, which returns early if `embed_by_username` user is missing). But `spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb` stubs `retrieved_recently?` in the “valid host” examples and only asserts whether `perform_retrieve` is called, so the Redis throttle behavior, bypass, and downstream branches mentioned are indeed left untested. This is a concrete test coverage concern created by the new logic, not a runtime defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: poll_feed_spec tests only the gating via mock expectation, never the feed-processing body: RSS parsing, the url fallback for Atom tag-URI ids, CGI.unescapeHTML on scrubbed content (raises NoMethodError on Atom entries with no content element, killing the hourly job with retry: false), and the silent return when the configured username doesn't exist

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only asserts `Jobs::PollFeed#execute` gates calling `poll_feed` based on settings, and does not exercise `poll_feed` itself (SimpleRSS parsing, `url = i.id` fallback, `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, or the `return if user.blank?` path when the configured `embed_by_username` doesn’t exist). The claim about a potential `NoMethodError` comes from `i.content.scrub` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` (no nil-guard), but whether Atom entries actually have `content == nil` is not provable from the diff alone, making this more of an untested/edge-case robustness concern than a strictly verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: TopicEmbed.import re-import with unchanged content (content_sha1 no-op branch) is untested, and the update test doesn't assert content_sha1 persistence or that no duplicate TopicEmbed/topic is created (unique index on embed_url makes a duplicate-creation regression a hard 500)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial branching in `TopicEmbed.import`: when an embed exists, it only revises the post and updates `content_sha1` if `content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`; otherwise it’s a no-op (returns the existing `post`). The new specs cover malformed URL, initial creation, and an update with changed contents, but they do not cover the unchanged-content no-op branch, nor do they assert that `topic_embeds` remains a single row for the `embed_url` or that `content_sha1` is persisted/updated (the update test only checks `post.cooked` matches new contents). This is a specific, diff-grounded test gap rather than a demonstrated defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: TopicEmbed.import_remote has no test at all (readability options, doc.title fallback)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial new behavior in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (uses `ruby-readability`, constructs `Readability::Document` with specific `tags`/`attributes`, and falls back to `opts[:title] || doc.title` before calling `TopicEmbed.import`). The added specs cover `.import` and URL absolutization, but there is no spec exercising `.import_remote`’s readability parsing, option handling, or title fallback. Given this method is now used by `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` and the Disqus import task, the lack of direct tests is a concrete review gap (not a defect by itself).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls port handling untested for non-80/443 ports and scheme-less URLs

adjudication.rationale: TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls builds a prefix including a non-default port (`prefix << ":#{uri.port}" if uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443`), but the added spec in `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` only asserts absolutization for a default-port URL (`http://eviltrout.com/123`) and does not cover non-80/443 ports. However, the mention of “scheme-less URLs” is largely moot in this diff because `TopicEmbed.import` immediately returns unless the URL matches `/^https?\:\/\//`, so scheme-less inputs won’t reach `absolutize_urls` via the shown call paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: New job Jobs::RetrieveTopic has no spec covering the Discourse::InvalidParameters raise on blank embed_url, the user lookup, and forwarding no_throttle: user.try(:staff?) (the security-relevant staff/non-staff throttle branch)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb` with nontrivial branching: it raises `Discourse::InvalidParameters` when `args[:embed_url]` is blank, conditionally looks up `User` by `args[:user_id]`, and forwards `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)` into `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve`. adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Client-side embed code (embed.js iframe injection and postMessage resize handshake including the discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) origin check and echoing request.referer) has no qunit/JS coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new client-side embedding behavior in `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` (DOM iframe injection, `window.addEventListener('message', ...)` resize handling, and an origin check via `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`) plus a corresponding postMessage sender in `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb` (posting to `request.referer`).
