adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: disqus.thor import rewritten to fetch each thread's live remote URL via TopicEmbed.import_remote (and --category option removed) with zero test or spec coverage for this behavioral change to a data-migration tool

adjudication.rationale: The diff rewrites the Disqus import task to create the topic by fetching/parsing each thread’s live URL (`post = TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`) and removes the `--category` option (`method_option :category` and related logic deleted) in `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`. The added specs cover `TopicEmbed`, `TopicRetriever`, `EmbedController`, and `Jobs::PollFeed`, but there is no spec or test added for the Thor task’s new behavior or the option removal, despite this being a nontrivial behavioral change to a migration/import tool.

adjudication_records.issue_text: External HTML rendered completely unsanitized: Post#cook returns raw verbatim when cook_method == :raw_html, skipping the entire cooking pipeline including sanitization, and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, causing stored XSS on the forum's origin (app/models/post.rb:131-134, app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Post.cook_methods` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, explicitly bypassing the normal cooking pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook`) that would otherwise sanitize/transform HTML (app/models/post.rb). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` using RSS/readability HTML content (app/models/topic_embed.rb), and the embed UI renders it using `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). The included spec asserts `post.cooked == post.raw`, confirming unsanitized HTML is rendered. This enables stored XSS if the imported HTML contains dangerous tags/attributes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unescaped URL interpolated into stored HTML in TopicEmbed: the imported-from footer builds HTML by string concatenation with the untrusted url, allowing attribute breakout via quotes or '>' and resulting in stored raw HTML (app/models/topic_embed.rb:8)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends an HTML footer via string interpolation: `"#{url}"` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). The only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes or `>` in the remainder of the string, so an attacker-controlled `url` could break out of the `href` attribute and inject arbitrary HTML/JS. This HTML is then persisted as `raw` and rendered with `cook_method: :raw_html` (Post#cook returns `raw`), and the embed view uses `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, making it a stored XSS vector grounded in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CGI.unescapeHTML actively de-escapes untrusted feed content before storage in PollFeed, converting properly escaped entities like <script> into live script tags and defeating any downstream sanitization layer (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:33)

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, feed item content is explicitly de-escaped via `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` before being passed into `TopicEmbed.import`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly for `raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. This means escaped entities like `<script>` from an untrusted feed can become literal `<script>` tags stored/served as-is (e.g., in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` using `raw post.cooked`), creating an XSS vulnerability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Reverse-direction origin check in embed client: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` tests whether the incoming origin is a substring of discourseUrl instead of validating e.origin against discourseUrl, a known-broken pattern that also misbehaves with trailing slashes or paths (app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17)

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js the message handler validates origin with `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`, which is only a substring check against the configured URL string, not an exact origin match. This can allow unintended origins if `discourseUrl` contains the origin as a substring (e.g., extra path/query text), and it also fails to robustly normalize/compare origins (scheme/port). A strict comparison against the parsed origin of `discourseUrl` would be required for correct security behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicRetriever synchronously instantiates the scheduled PollFeed job and calls execute({}) directly, a separation-of-concerns violation where a single user-triggered embed request causes a full inline feed fetch/parse/import of every item (lib/topic_retriever.rb:38)

adjudication.rationale: Verified: in lib/topic_retriever.rb#perform_retrieve, when SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled? is true it directly runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline (rather than enqueueing), then only afterwards checks whether a TopicEmbed now exists. Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed parses the entire feed and iterates `rss.items.each` importing each item, so a single embed retrieval path can synchronously trigger a full feed fetch/parse/import, which is an architecture/performance separation-of-concerns issue rather than a strict correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Embed loading page reloads forever with no failure path: if RetrieveTopic fails (network error, unparseable feed, unresolved embed_by_username) and PollFeed is retry: false, the iframe shows 'Loading...' and reloads every 30 seconds indefinitely with no backoff, terminal state, or error feedback (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:5-9, app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:9)

adjudication.rationale: When no TopicEmbed exists, `EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` and renders `embed/loading` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:14-18). The loading template unconditionally reloads the iframe every 30s (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:6-9) and there is no terminal/error state. If retrieval never produces a `TopicEmbed` (e.g., `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` returns early when `embed_by_username` user is blank, or remote fetch/parse fails), the iframe will stay in an infinite reload loop with no user feedback. The mention of `PollFeed` being `retry: false` is ancillary, but the “no failure path → infinite loading” behavior is directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed assumes i.content is present for all feed items: `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError on feeds whose entries lack content (e.g. Atom entries with only summary), and combined with retry: false one malformed item aborts the entire poll cycle (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:33)

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the new code unconditionally calls `i.content.scrub` (`content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`). If `i.content` is nil for any feed item, this will raise NoMethodError and abort the job. The job is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so a single such exception would stop that polling run without retries.

adjudication_records.issue_text: skip_validations option leaks from embed import into the generic revision path: PostRevisor exposes `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` as a general-purpose escape hatch allowing any caller to silently bypass all validations on post edits, with nothing marking the revised post as system-authored (lib/post_revisor.rb:85)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes PostRevisor to save with `validate: !@opts[:skip_validations]` (lib/post_revisor.rb) and the new embed update path explicitly calls `revisor.revise!(..., skip_validations: true, ...)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). That does introduce a general-purpose bypass knob on PostRevisor with no additional auditing/marking in this diff, but the diff does not show any untrusted caller being able to set this option directly, so it’s more of an architectural/safety concern than a directly verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicated 'find the embed author user' logic in TopicRetriever and PollFeed: identical User lookup by embed_by_username duplicated in two components, both silently returning nil and doing nothing when the setting doesn't match a real user, with no logging or error on misconfiguration (lib/topic_retriever.rb:50, app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:26)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows duplicated logic to resolve the “embed author” user from the `embed_by_username` setting: `user = User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first` appears in `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:26-27) and in `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` (lib/topic_retriever.rb:50-52). In both places, if no matching user is found, the method simply `return`s (PollFeed: `return if user.blank?`; TopicRetriever: `return if user.blank?`) with no logging/exception, so a misconfiguration causes silent no-op behavior. This is a real, diff-grounded maintainability/operability issue, but not a strictly verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import mutates its caller's contents argument via `contents << ...`, so the caller's variable silently includes the appended footer after the call — pure side-effect coupling in a public model API (app/models/topic_embed.rb:8)

adjudication.rationale: Verified: `TopicEmbed.import` appends to the passed-in `contents` string in-place via `contents << "\n<hr>..."` (app/models/topic_embed.rb), which mutates the caller’s object. This is a concrete, diff-grounded side-effect in a public API and can cause surprising coupling if callers reuse the same string after calling `import`. In the shown call sites (e.g., `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` assigns `content` then immediately passes it; `import_remote` passes `doc.content`), it likely won’t break current behavior, but it is still an important API/maintainability concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus import task interface silently broken: the --category option is removed without deprecation or version bump, breaking existing scripted invocations with -c, and the task's semantics changed from importing stored Disqus content to fetching the live thread URL via TopicEmbed.import_remote, coupling a one-shot migration tool to network availability (lib/tasks/disqus.thor:114)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `--category/-c` Thor option and the related category_id handling in `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` (lines around the removed `method_option :category` and subsequent `Category.where(...)` logic), and it changes behavior from creating a post directly via `PostCreator` to calling `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`, which performs a live `open(url)` fetch. This is a real, diff-grounded backward-incompatible interface/semantics change for scripted invocations, but it’s not clearly a correctness defect in the application itself (and Thor would typically error on an unknown `-c` rather than “silently” ignoring it).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Embed client assumes #discourse-comments exists: no null check on document.getElementById('discourse-comments'), so a snippet pasted with the wrong element id throws instead of degrading gracefully (app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:5-10)

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, `comments` is set via `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then immediately used as `comments.appendChild(iframe)` with no guard. If the host page includes the script but does not have an element with id `discourse-comments`, `comments` will be null and the script will throw a runtime error, breaking graceful behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Editing already-applied migration 20131223171005_create_top_topics to add force: true to create_table, which will DROP TABLE IF EXISTS on re-run and silently destroy all top_topics data with no rollback path

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` from `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails this will drop the table if it already exists before creating it, which can cause data loss in scenarios where the migration is re-run or the table exists unexpectedly. However, under normal Rails migration flow an already-applied migration is not re-executed, so this is more a migration-safety/process concern than a guaranteed runtime defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_column :posts, :cook_method with default and null: false on the large posts table triggers a full table rewrite under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock in PostgreSQL, blocking all reads/writes with no disable_ddl_transaction! or batching, causing production outage risk on upgrades

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new migration `db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb` with `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. On PostgreSQL versions prior to 11, adding a column with a non-null default is implemented via a full table rewrite and takes an `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock for the duration, which can block reads/writes on the (potentially large) `posts` table. This migration does not use `disable_ddl_transaction!`, batching, or a safer multi-step backfill pattern, so the review concern about upgrade/outage risk is diff-grounded (even though it is an operational/migration concern rather than an application correctness bug).

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_table :topic_embeds with force: true will drop and recreate the table if re-run after embeddings exist, destroying the embed_url → topic mapping and causing duplicate re-imports with no down-guard or pre-drop data check

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`, which in Rails will drop an existing `topic_embeds` table before recreating it. In normal operation migrations are not re-run, so this doesn’t create an immediate/runtime defect from the diff alone. However, it is a concrete migration-safety concern because if the table exists for any reason (e.g., a partially applied migration history, manual table creation, or an operator mistake), running this migration would destroy existing `topic_embeds` rows (and thus the `embed_url`→`topic_id` mapping) without any safeguard.

adjudication_records.issue_text: t.string :embed_url maps to varchar(255), so long real-world URLs will raise ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid on insert, aborting the PollFeed job mid-iteration (retry: false) and permanently skipping remaining feed items with no later migration widening the column

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` defines `t.string :embed_url, null: false` with no `limit`, so under Rails defaults this is a 255-byte varchar. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` iterates feed items and calls `TopicEmbed.import`, which does `TopicEmbed.create!` with `embed_url: url` and has no rescue around the loop. If a feed item has a URL longer than the column limit, the insert can fail and raise, aborting the job mid-iteration; the job is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so remaining items would be skipped until the next run. The diff shows no migration widening `embed_url` (e.g., to `:text` or a larger limit).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS: externally-authored RSS/Atom feed HTML imported via raw_html cook path with zero sanitization, bypassing the entire cooking pipeline and rendering executable HTML via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in embed/best.html.erb and topic pages

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `:raw_html` cook path that returns `raw` directly in `Post#cook` (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`), explicitly bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `Jobs::PollFeed` imports externally-authored `i.content` from an RSS/Atom feed (only `CGI.unescapeHTML(...scrub)`; no sanitization) and `TopicEmbed.import` creates a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. The embed UI then renders this HTML with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, so malicious HTML/JS from the feed could be stored and executed (stored XSS).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Readability import path strips script tags but does not filter URL schemes, so `href="javascript:..."` on allowed `<a>` tags survives into cooked HTML

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, `Readability::Document` is invoked with `attributes: %w[href src]` and allowed tags including `a` (`lib/topic_embed.rb`), but there is no subsequent sanitization of URL schemes. The imported HTML is stored as `raw` and marked `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which makes `Post#cook` return `raw` and bypass the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline (`app/models/post.rb`). The embed view then renders it with `raw post.cooked` (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`). Therefore an `<a href="javascript:...">` from the readability output would survive into rendered HTML.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unescaped URL interpolated into href attribute in TopicEmbed.import (topic_embed.rb:11); URL validated only by a prefix regex, allowing quotes/HTML to break out of the attribute and inject persistent HTML

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, `url` is interpolated directly into an HTML attribute without escaping: `contents << "... %{link: \"#{url}\"}"`. The only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which allows attacker-controlled characters (e.g. a single quote) after the prefix to break out of `href='...'` and inject arbitrary HTML/JS. This is especially dangerous because imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, `Post#cook` returns `raw`, and the embed view renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, making the injection persistent and rendered as-is.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unauthenticated /embed/best acts as a job-enqueue and outbound-fetch amplifier; the Referer header check provides no real protection and per-URL throttling is bypassed by cycling URLs, flooding Sidekiq, performing outbound fetches, and writing Redis keys

adjudication.rationale: `EmbedController#best` is publicly reachable (`get 'embed/best'`) and, when no `TopicEmbed` exists, unconditionally enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, embed_url: ...)` for the caller. `ensure_embeddable` only checks `request.referer` host against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, but the Referer header can be spoofed by non-browser clients, so it is not strong protection against direct abuse. In `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, `TopicRetriever#retrieve` applies only a per-URL Redis throttle (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}` for 60s), which can be bypassed by cycling many distinct URLs on the allowed host. Each unique URL can then trigger `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)` which performs `open(url).read` (outbound fetch) and may create DB records, enabling Sidekiq flooding plus outbound-request amplification and Redis key growth as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed fails silently and permanently: retry: false with no error handling means nil feed fields (i.content, i.title) crash the run, one malformed item skips all subsequent items forever, and blank titles bypass validations due to skip_validations: true

adjudication.rationale: In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, each RSS item is processed without any per-item validation or rescue. The code calls `i.content.scrub` (`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`), which will raise `NoMethodError` if `i.content` is `nil`, aborting the whole job and skipping all remaining items for that run. Additionally, `TopicEmbed.import` uses `PostCreator.new(..., skip_validations: true, ...)` (`app/models/topic_embed.rb`), so a `nil`/blank `i.title` would bypass normal validations and can create malformed topics/posts. The job also has `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so failures won’t be retried by Sidekiq.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import raises RecordNotUnique on concurrent first-retrievals of the same embed_url against the unique index, killing the remaining feed items for that run

adjudication.rationale: `TopicEmbed.import` does a non-atomic check-then-create: `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and if blank it later calls `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction. With the unique index `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`, concurrent first imports of the same `embed_url` can both observe `blank?` and then one `create!` will raise `RecordNotUnique` (no rescue shown). In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, this exception would abort the `rss.items.each` loop, potentially preventing remaining feed items from being processed in that run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Embed loading page reloads forever when retrieval silently no-ops (e.g. blank embed_by_username or fetch failure), generating steady background load and outbound fetches with no surfaced misconfiguration

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no `topic_id` exists it always enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `embed/loading`. The loading template (`app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`) unconditionally reloads the page every 30 seconds (`setTimeout(... document.location.reload() ...)`) with no terminal error state. If retrieval never creates a `TopicEmbed` (e.g., `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` returns early when `embed_by_username` doesn't resolve to a user, or remote fetch/parsing fails), the client will keep reloading indefinitely and continue triggering repeated requests/job enqueues, creating steady background load without surfacing the misconfiguration/failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic SETNX/EXPIRE in TopicRetriever (lib/topic_retriever.rb:31-37) can permanently blacklist an embed URL if the process crashes between the two calls, since the key persists with no TTL

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle key is created with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and only then given a TTL via a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process dies/crashes between these two calls, the key can be left without an expiry, causing `setnx` to return false on all future attempts and making `retrieved_recently?` return true forever for that embed URL (permanent throttling/blacklisting).

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js origin check uses indexOf substring match instead of strict origin comparison, allowing spoofed origins that are substrings of discourseUrl to post messages
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same security flaw: validating postMessage origin using indexOf/substring matching rather than strict origin comparison, which can be bypassed by a malicious domain containing the expected domain as a substring (e.g., evil-discourseUrl.com).

adjudication_records.issue_text: request.referer interpolated raw into a JS single-quoted string in embed.html.erb; Rails html_escape does not escape single quotes, allowing Referer header to break out of the JS string literal
matched_golden_ids: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that request.referer is interpolated into a JavaScript string without proper escaping, specifically noting single-quote escaping issues that allow breaking out of the JS literal and enabling XSS. This matches the golden issue of unescaped Referer header leading to XSS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key in poll_feed.rb is dead code: never read or written, no If-Modified-Since/etag handling, so every run re-parses the full feed and the first poll imports the entire backlog

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `def feed_key` is defined but never referenced by `execute` or `poll_feed`, so it is dead code in this diff. Also, `poll_feed` always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates `rss.items` with no conditional GET (etag/If-Modified-Since) or persisted “last seen” state, meaning every run reparses the full feed; on first run it will attempt to import every item present in the feed. While duplicates are largely prevented by `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`/unique index and SHA1 comparison, the lack of incremental fetching/state is a concrete inefficiency/scope gap rather than a directly verifiable functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitive host comparison in embed_controller.rb and topic_retriever.rb rejects legitimate embedders; URI.host preserves case and excludes port, so differing casing or a port in embeddable_host breaks the comparison

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds strict string equality checks between `URI(...).host` and `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` in both `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` (`URI(request.referer||'').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`) and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` (`SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host`). There is no normalization (e.g., downcasing, stripping whitespace) and the comparison uses only `.host` (not port), so if the setting is configured with a different case or includes a port (e.g. `example.com:3000`), legitimate requests would be rejected as 'invalid referer host' / treated as invalid_host.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus import task silently drops threads whose link is not http(s); import returns nil and the if post.present? check skips the thread and all its comments with no warning

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the import now does `post = TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` and then only imports comments when `post.present?`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `TopicEmbed.import`, which immediately returns `nil` unless `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` (in `TopicEmbed.import`). Therefore any Disqus thread whose `t[:link]` is non-http(s) will result in `post == nil` and the entire thread's comments will be skipped with no explicit warning/error beyond the earlier `puts`.
